validity.recommendation: Verify final as-built length; consider noting 115 km (post-completion source) vs 130 km (pre-construction design source) rather than carrying only the design figure.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own two cited sources for this row disagree on length. powernews.cc (dated 2020-04-13, PPC announcing it 'has begun implementing'/'will begin immediately' the line, 15-month construction window) states the design length as 130 km ('خط بوتاجاز دمياط – طنطا بطول 130 كيلو متر') -- this is the source GEM's LengthKnown=130.00 currently cites. youm7.com (dated 2021-12-26, covering the port's first LPG carrier arrival that 'inaugurates' the line) states verbatim 'يبلغ طول خط الغاز دمياط – طنطا (محافظة الغربية) حوالى 115 كم' = 'the length of the Damietta-Tanta gas line (Gharbia governorate) is about 115 km.' That is a ~13% disagreement (115 vs 130 km) between a pre-construction design estimate and a post-completion inauguration report on the SAME named line, and the later (completion-stage) figure is arguably the more authoritative one for as-built length, yet GEM carries only the earlier design figure. Not confident enough either way to force a value change -- flagging as a material spec disagreement per the corroboration standard rather than silently passing it. Diameter (12 in) and cost (600 million EGP) are NOT in dispute -- powernews.cc is the only source giving those, and no other source contradicts them.

validity.recommendation: No action needed on Cost; existing_ref_checks flag is a false alarm from digit-vs-word mismatch, not a real sourcing gap.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence: strongly confirmed. Two independent, genuinely distinct Egyptian outlets (youm7.com, a major mainstream daily, and powernews.cc, an energy-trade site) both name this exact line 'خط دمياط – طنطا' (Damietta-Tanta line) at different project stages -- powernews.cc (2020-04-13) covers Petroleum Pipelines Co. (PPC) beginning construction, and youm7.com (2021-12-26) covers the completion/inauguration event (Damietta port receiving its first dedicated LPG carrier for the line). This is not a GEM-only entity. Classification: 'transmission' PipelineType is reasonable -- this is a 115-130 km trunk line moving imported LPG from a coastal receiving terminal to an inland distribution hub (Tanta/Gharbia) as part of what powernews.cc calls the 'national butane network' (استكمال الشبكة القومية للبيوتاجاز), not a short gathering/feeder line. Fuel=LPG and Status=operating are both consistent with both sources. Duplicate check: no other pipeline in the 46-row Egypt-oil roster shares this name, route, or endpoints -- no duplicate/relabel concern. Cost cell: the worklist's existing_ref_checks flagged Cost (600000000 EGP) against powernews.cc as 'value not found' because the verifier does substring matching on digit strings, but the article states the figure in words, verbatim: 'باستثمارات 600 مليون جنيه' (investments of 600 million EGP) = 600,000,000 EGP exactly. This is a prose/digit-format mismatch, not an unsupported value -- Cost is in fact well supported by its existing ref and needs no change. Operator note (attribution, not flagged as a concern): youm7.com's inauguration article names 'United Gas Derivatives Company' (الشركة المتحدة لمشتقات الغاز) as the entity managing the Damietta Port RECEIVING TERMINAL, which is distinct from Petroleum Pipelines Co. (PPC), which powernews.cc names as the entity executing/building the pipeline itself. This is consistent with the normal Egyptian midstream split (import-terminal operator vs. cross-country pipeline operator) rather than a contradiction of GEM's Operator=Petroleum Pipelines Co, but it is worth knowing UGDC exists in the sourcing so it is not mistakenly substituted in later.

fills.researcher_notes: youm7.com's Dec 2021 inauguration article describes Damietta Port's terminal (operated by United Gas Derivatives Company) receiving the imported LPG carrier that supplies this line onward to Tanta -- confirms Damietta Port as the origin/feed point for the LPG moved by this pipeline. Medium tier: single strong source naming the port as the feed point; no second source discusses upstream fuel sourcing specifically.

powernews.cc's headline and body explicitly name 'أنابيب البترول' (Petroleum Pipelines Co., PPC) as the company executing/building the Damietta-Tanta line, consistent with PPC's standard role as Egypt's cross-country product-pipeline operator (per scope guidance). Medium tier: this source documents PPC at the construction stage, not a later operations confirmation, and no second source independently names an operator (youm7's 2021 piece names only the receiving-terminal operator, UGDC, which is a distinct node -- see validity notes).

summary: P7365 (Damietta Port-Tanta LPG Pipeline) confirmed real, correctly classified, no duplicate in the 46-row roster; one spec concern flagged (GEM's own two cited sources disagree 115 km vs 130 km on length -- not resolved, needs a human call); Cost 'value not found' flag is a false alarm (digit-vs-word mismatch, article says '600 مليون جنيه' = 600,000,000 EGP); added refs for FuelSource and Operator (both MISSING_REF, both medium tier).
